summary:
1. The audit stands (625 requirements: 288 done, 198 partial, 124 missing, 11 diverged, 4 unverifiable): the engine is sound, the front door is not. Nothing calls the extractors, a build never cooks a source, Open versus Import is on no screen.
2. Gap level is complete: every non-done requirement except five superseded or unverifiable ones is named by a gap (checked by script). Wave level was not: briefs left out the origin.how write, a byte-identical source save, .gitattributes, a hover step in the shots machinery, Restore original, and the explorer-menu and archive files an Import wave must edit.
3. Order was wrong for rule (c): engine, cook and reload came first, the screens a user meets (start page, New project, the five major project defects) came after import and cook. Now P1 front door, P2 project majors and P3 import engine start together after L; H3 follows P2; the Import UI (P4) follows P2 and P3.
4. Size: nine waves bundled 5 to 7 unrelated items (old P2, P3, P5, P7, P8, P9, P11, P12, P13). The plan is now 32 waves, each one subsystem. The claim that P2, P3 and P5 could run together was false (P5 needed P2).
5. Missing: the owner's last two steps (re-verify, then draft weapon, particle, map and other views) had no wave: P31 and P32. Shots could not draw drop hover, a running job or four project screens: folded into P1.
6. Wrongly parked as author mode: five diverged requirements (the model JSON should say what glTF cannot, re-split with a report, DDS beside the glb). Not all of it is held back: P12 builds it behind ruling R21 and leaves vertex-layout presets out.
7. Held back: the LOD decimator adds a geometry, a non-goal in Mesh_Interchange.md, so P30 needs a ruling; P29 (cap default, replace mode) and P12 too. Nothing else depends on them.
8. Duplicates fixed: old P4 and H2 both refreshed a preview after a recook (now P8, which H2 uses); ReplaceTexture repeated H2's drop (P20 exposes it); the clothes dump repeated L's emitter kind; the rules reuse L's rule shape.
9. Import is not two meanings but five (Import Texture, Import glTF, Import File, the archive drop hint, the drop undo label): P4 renames the other four.
10. Concurrency checked by script on the file lists: no two waves that may run together share a file, except one registration line in workbench/mod.rs between H3 and P4 (read H3's lane diff first; H3 and H2 lists are guessed from their briefs).

waves.title: Import engine: a game file becomes a source on disk
waves.brief: Read first: Source_Format_Design.md (folder and manifest, Layout per format, Commit policy), or-source asset.rs, textures.rs extract, models.rs extract_drawable and extract_drawables, or-project adopt.rs (the bounded walk to copy), or-cli project.rs and what L changed in or-cli. Build with no UI, in or-source module game_import and suite tests/game_import.rs: (1) A kind table from extension to source kind with rows for .ytd textures, .ydr drawable, .ydd drawables and nothing else; any other extension yields Kept{reason} and the engine can copy a Kept file unchanged under <project>/files/ (R3), so P10 adds rows rather than reshaping this. (2) import(project_root, input): bytes plus a virtual name plus origin facts (from_game, virtual_path, game_build), or a file path, or a folder walked recursively (skip build/, vfs/, hidden folders, nested *.src and *.openrage-proj; adopt's file and depth bounds; say what a bound left out). (3) Extract into a staging folder and rename to sources/<name>.<kind>.src only on success; never write into an existing folder: a name taken by another origin gets _2, _3 (R1); the same origin.virtual_path plus sha256 (or the same sha256 for a loose file) reports AlreadyASource and writes nothing; never modify the input; record origin.how (extracted or imported), origin.sha256 and game_build. (4) Return a per-file Report (Made, AlreadyASource, Kept, Refused, each with a reason sentence), the created folders and a digest of each tree, so a caller can undo exactly them while untouched. (5) git.rs: a managed .gitignore block (build/, vfs/, every from_game source) and a .gitattributes block marking source binaries as binary (Git LFS only if the person opts in), each between markers, idempotent, other lines untouched. (6) In asset.rs: keep notes out of the recook digest, add reid(folder) giving a copied source a new id, and Source::save rewriting every JSON file canonically so a save of an unchanged source is byte-identical. (7) openrage-cli project import <project> <paths> [--from-game] [--json] in a new import.rs prints the report.

Say which corpus suites ran and which skipped.

waves.title: Only sources in a project: create or import, and references for what stays outside
waves.brief: Owner ruling of 2026-10-09, to build and not to reopen. A project holds no compiled game file. A game file that enters a project, by any door (the Project view's Add, a drop, the Wardrobe, Replace model or texture, a folder), is decompiled at once into its source, and a source is platform-free: the build compiles it for the platform or platforms the build states. There are two ways in. CREATE: right-click in Content offers New for each kind (a texture dictionary among them), an empty source that is then filled. IMPORT: a game file (a .ytd is decompiled), an asset.json, a source folder such as a .textures.src taken as it is, or a folder scanned recursively. The one place a file that is not a source of this project may be named is a REFERENCE: something a content needs and does not own, for example the cloth (.yld) of a garment, a model or a texture. A reference is one of three things: a file of this project (a source), a file of another project (a popup asks 'Import this file into the project, or only reference it?'), or an id typed by hand (a name or hash) for a file the user does not have. It is chosen through a custom picker with a good UX (this project's contents first, search, recent files, Browse for another project or a file, a field for an id). The rule is for every kind, not only textures and garments, and every later view (weapons, particles, maps) uses it. Read first: Workbench_UX_Design.md (Import, Content, the Wardrobe), Project_Model_Design.md and the links module of or-project (a link is a whole folder; a reference is one member), the import engine of P3 and the report of P4, and the P22 section (a picture dropped on a garment was compiled to a Legacy .ytd at the drop: that is the defect this wave removes). Start with an audit in the pull request: for each door list what it stores today (compiled file kept, or source), and for the Wardrobe what its pack holds. Build in order: (1) one rule at the door in the import engine: every file with a source form is decompiled; a kind with no source form yet stays in Files and is named in the report; no door writes a compiled file into a project. (2) Create commands per kind in Content's menu and the command palette, with an empty source that validates. (3) A reference as data in the project file, with its three forms, resolved when the plan is made: a reference to a source of this project follows a rename, a reference to another project is stored by path as links are, an id-only reference is written into the build as the id and the plan says in a sentence that the file is not in the project; an unresolved reference is a Problem with Locate. (4) The picker as a reusable dialog (egui, keyboard first, narrow windows), its two popups (import or only reference; the id field), and the Link cloth and Replace model buttons of the Wardrobe using it. (5) The Wardrobe: a picture dropped on a garment becomes an authored textures source of the garment (no DDS until it compiles, the build compiles it for each platform it states), the TARGET constant of images.rs goes, and a garment's model, textures and cloth are sources or references; where the pack's compiled files are still read in place (a pack adopted from disk), say so in the pull request and keep that path read-only. Report what the Wardrobe still keeps compiled and why, as the follow-up list for P24.

Undo of an import deletes folders. It removes only the folders the import created, checks each tree's digest first and refuses when one was edited; a wrong delete loses a person's work.

Cooking inside a build costs time and memory and must be deterministic (two builds byte-identical) or the diff and the reproducibility line lie. Skipping unchanged from_game content relies on the exact-copy path coming first; a re-encoded texture never matches origin.sha256.
